print-head.definition: The moving assembly that carries the nozzle and related parts used to place printing material.
print-head.exampleUsage: The print head moves across the machine while each layer is formed.

build-plate.definition: The flat surface that supports an object while a 3D printer builds it layer by layer.
build-plate.exampleUsage: The trained operator checked the build plate according to the printer’s maintenance instructions.

filament-spool.definition: A reel that holds printing filament and allows it to feed into a 3D printer.
filament-spool.exampleUsage: The filament spool sat on the printer’s compatible holder.

extruder.definition: The printer assembly that grips, feeds, and directs filament toward the heated printing end.
extruder.exampleUsage: The extruder feeds filament steadily during the print.

nozzle.definition: The small opening through which a filament printer deposits melted material.

stepper-motor.definition: An electric motor that turns in small controlled steps to position machine parts accurately.
stepper-motor.exampleUsage: A stepper motor moves the printer carriage to precise positions.

belt.definition: A flexible loop that transfers movement between pulleys in the printer.

guide-rail.definition: A straight rail that keeps a moving printer part traveling along a controlled path.
guide-rail.exampleUsage: The carriage slides smoothly along the guide rail.

cooling-fan.definition: A fan that moves air to cool printer parts or freshly deposited material during printing.
cooling-fan.exampleUsage: The cooling fan helps the new layer become firm quickly.

lcd-screen.definition: A liquid-crystal display that shows printer information, menus, and settings.
lcd-screen.exampleUsage: The LCD screen displayed the selected printing settings.

pla-filament.definition: A common thermoplastic printing material made mainly from polylactic acid and valued for easy printing.
pla-filament.exampleUsage: The class used PLA filament for a simple prototype.
pla-filament.arabicTranslation: خيط PLA من حمض متعدد اللاكتيك

abs-filament.definition: A tough thermoplastic printing material made from acrylonitrile, butadiene, and styrene.
abs-filament.exampleUsage: The enclosure helps reduce warping when printing with ABS filament.
abs-filament.arabicTranslation: خيط ABS من أكريلونيتريل بوتادين ستايرين

petg-filament.definition: A thermoplastic printing filament made from glycol-modified polyethylene terephthalate.
petg-filament.exampleUsage: PETG filament is useful for many practical printed parts.

resin.definition: A liquid printing material that hardens when exposed to suitable light.

nylon.definition: A strong synthetic plastic material that can be used as flexible, durable 3D-printing filament.
nylon.exampleUsage: Nylon can be used when a printed part needs strength and flexibility.

flexible-filament.definition: An elastic printing material that can bend or stretch after it has been printed.
flexible-filament.exampleUsage: Flexible filament is useful for making soft grips and protective parts.

wood-filament.definition: A composite printing material that mixes a plastic base with wood particles to create a wood-like finish.
wood-filament.exampleUsage: The wood filament gave the model a natural-looking surface.

metal-filament.definition: A composite printing material that mixes a plastic base with metal particles for a metallic appearance or added weight.
metal-filament.exampleUsage: The metal filament made the decorative part look more like real metal.

support-material.definition: Temporary printed material that holds overhangs or difficult shapes in place and is removed after printing.
support-material.exampleUsage: The printer added support material beneath the model's overhang.

glue-stick.definition: A solid adhesive in a twist-up tube used for clean, controlled gluing.
glue-stick.exampleUsage: The student used a glue stick to attach the paper template.

computer.definition: An electronic device used to prepare designs and control printing tasks.
computer.exampleUsage: Omar opens the design on his computer before sending it to the printer.

3d-software.definition: Computer software used to create, prepare, or manage three-dimensional models for printing.
3d-software.exampleUsage: The designer opened the model in 3D software before printing it.

mouse.definition: A hand-operated electronic device that controls the coordinates of a cursor on your computer screen as you move it around on a pad.
mouse.exampleUsage: Nadia uses the mouse to rotate the model on the screen.

graphics-tablet.definition: A flat computer input device that lets a person draw or write with an electronic pen.
graphics-tablet.exampleUsage: The designer sketched the new shape on a graphics tablet.

ruler.definition: A straight tool used for measuring and drawing lines.
ruler.exampleUsage: Omar measures the model's length with a ruler.

caliper.definition: An instrument for measuring the distance between two points.
caliper.exampleUsage: Nadia checks the printed part's width with a caliper.

protractor.definition: Drafting instrument used to draw or measure angles.
protractor.exampleUsage: Omar uses a protractor to check the angle in his sketch.

grid-paper.definition: Paper printed with evenly spaced lines that form squares for drawing, measuring, or planning.
grid-paper.exampleUsage: The student sketched the design on grid paper before modeling it.

sketchbook.definition: A book of blank pages for drawing or writing.

reference-model.definition: A model used as a guide when designing or comparing a new object.

sandpaper.definition: Stiff paper coated with powdered emery or sand.

file.definition: A hand tool with a rough surface used to shape or smooth material.
file.exampleUsage: Nadia uses a file to smooth the edge of the printed part.

craft-knife.definition: A small sharp cutting tool used for precise craft and model-making work.
craft-knife.exampleUsage: The instructor keeps the craft knife with the model-finishing tools.

pliers.definition: A hand tool with two handles used for gripping or cutting.
pliers.exampleUsage: The technician grips the small component with pliers.

tweezers.definition: A small tool consisting of two pointed arms used for picking up small objects or plucking hairs.
tweezers.exampleUsage: Nadia picks up the tiny part with tweezers.

paint.definition: A colored substance applied to a surface to decorate or protect it.

paintbrush.definition: A tool with hairs used to spread paint.
paintbrush.exampleUsage: Omar applies color to the model with a paintbrush.

primer.definition: The first or preliminary coat of paint or size applied to a surface.

acetone.definition: A volatile, flammable solvent stored and handled under appropriate professional controls.
acetone.exampleUsage: The technician checked the safety data and material compatibility before any authorized use of acetone.

uv-curing-lamp.definition: A lamp that produces ultraviolet light to harden UV-sensitive resin.
uv-curing-lamp.exampleUsage: The finished resin part was placed under a UV curing lamp.

figurine.definition: A small carved or molded figure.

phone-case.definition: A protective cover designed to fit around a mobile phone.

gear.definition: A wheel with teeth that fit into another gear to transfer movement.

bracket.definition: A support or mounting piece used to hold parts of a 3D printer or printed assembly in position.

keychain.definition: A ring or short chain used to hold keys together.

cookie-cutter.definition: A shaped tool used to cut dough or soft material into a particular outline.
cookie-cutter.exampleUsage: Nadia designs a star-shaped cookie cutter in the modeling software.

whistle.definition: A small object blown to make a loud signal.

chess-piece.definition: One of the objects that players move on a chessboard.

architectural-model.definition: A physical scale representation of a building or architectural design.

workstation.definition: A work area equipped with the tools and equipment needed for a task.

storage-shelf.definition: A horizontal surface used for storing tools, materials, or finished parts.
storage-shelf.exampleUsage: The finished models are on the storage shelf.

ventilation-fan.definition: A fan that moves air into or out of a room or enclosure to improve ventilation.

fire-extinguisher.definition: A portable device that releases a substance used to put out a small fire.
fire-extinguisher.exampleUsage: A fire extinguisher is kept near the workshop exit for emergencies.

safety-glasses.definition: Protective eyewear worn to shield the eyes from particles, splashes, or other hazards.
safety-glasses.exampleUsage: Students wear safety glasses while working with tools and materials.

gloves.definition: Protective coverings worn on the hands while working with suitable tools or materials.

trash-bin.definition: A container used for collecting waste before it is removed.
trash-bin.exampleUsage: The workshop’s trash bin held the waste permitted under its disposal rules.

label-maker.definition: A small device that prints adhesive labels for identifying items.
label-maker.exampleUsage: Omar uses the label maker to identify the material boxes.

zip-bag.definition: A resealable plastic bag with a press-to-close or sliding zip seal.

desiccant-pack.definition: A small packet containing material that absorbs moisture from the surrounding air.

frame.definition: The structure that supports and holds the printer's parts in position.

fan.definition: A rotating device that moves air to cool or ventilate parts of the printer.
fan.exampleUsage: The fan moves air around the printed layers.

display.definition: A screen or panel that shows printer information, menus, and settings.

pla.definition: A common plastic filament used for making objects with a 3D printer.

abs.definition: Any of a class of composite plastics used to make car bodies and cases for computers and other appliances.

petg.definition: A strong, slightly flexible plastic filament used in 3D printing.

tpu.definition: A flexible plastic filament used to print bendable objects.

carbon-fiber.definition: A lightweight material made from extremely thin carbon strands arranged in a highly ordered structure. It is usually added to plastics and other materials to make composite parts stronger and stiffer.

wood-fill.definition: A 3D printing filament blended with wood particles for a woodlike finish.

design.definition: The act of working out the form of something (as by making a sketch or outline or plan).

slice.definition: To convert a 3D model into printable layers and machine instructions.
slice.exampleUsage: Nadia will slice the model before starting the print.

print.definition: To create a three-dimensional object by depositing or curing material layer by layer.

layer.definition: One thin level of material added during a 3D print.

support.definition: Temporary printed structures that hold overhangs or difficult shapes during printing.

infill.definition: The pattern of printed material inside an object that helps support its outer walls.

calibrate.definition: To adjust a printer or measuring tool so that it works accurately.

prototype.definition: An early model made to test the form, fit, or function of a design.

vase.definition: A container used to hold flowers or as a decorative object.
